summary: Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive 3D globe that makes NASA climate data easy to explore. Users click any country, choose from 36 Earth-system variables (temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, snow, radiation and more) from 2000 to 2022, and see how each variable changes over time. We process raw NASA GLDAS files with Python, compute country-level yearly values, and apply the Mann-Kendall test to detect statistically significant trends. The result is a simple click-and-explore tool for students, researchers and decision-makers, with no coding required, that turns complex NASA data into clear insights about environmental change.
details:
What it does: Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web app. Users spin a 3D globe, click a country, and explore 36 Earth-system variables from NASA GLDAS (2000-2022). For each variable they can see its value by year and whether the change over time is statistically significant.

How it works: We downloaded monthly NASA GLDAS Noah (GLDAS_NOAH025_M) data from NASA Earthdata. A Python pipeline (xarray, numpy, regionmask) aggregates the raw .nc4 files into country-level yearly values, and the Mann-Kendall test detects trends. A Streamlit and globe.gl interface presents the results.

Benefits and impact: It lowers the barrier to using NASA Earth data. Students, researchers and decision-makers can investigate environmental change in seconds, without coding.

Tools: Python, xarray, numpy, regionmask, geopandas, Streamlit, globe.gl, GitHub.

Creativity: a "become a data detective" workflow with guided questions and one-click demos (e.g. air temperature in Egypt).

AI disclosure: An AI assistant helped us write and debug parts of the code and draft text. The team reviewed, ran and tested everything.

Source code: https://github.com/muhamed-mosaed/nasa-space-apps
